title: GenWave Ad Pack Catalog Entry Metadata
description: The <slug>.meta.json shape for a kind:"ad-pack" entry (app repo SPEC F162.2, catalog-owned). Mirrors show-meta.schema.json's posture exactly (additionalProperties false — this document belongs entirely to the catalog, so an unrecognized field is a contributor mistake worth failing CI on) with the show-only `suggestedPersona` dropped: a pack of briefs suggests no DJ. No `license`/`sourceUrl` either, unlike an icon pack — an ad pack is ORIGINAL prose, dedicated CC0 like a persona card (the repo LICENSE), with nothing upstream to attribute; a pack adapting someone else's copy or naming real brands does not belong on this shelf at all (CONTRIBUTING's hard bans). The shelf card renders from the manifest's own `packName` plus `author`/`description`/`audience`/`added`/`bestFor`.
$comment: `added`'s pattern ends in (?![\s\S]), the same portable absolute-end-of-string anchor persona-meta.schema.json/theme-meta.schema.json/font-meta.schema.json document in full and repeat verbatim — repeated here too so this file stands alone.

author.description: Who wrote the briefs. Ad packs are open to community submission (the persona/show posture), so this is the contributor's own handle or name.

description.description: A short blurb introducing the pack's brand universe — shown on the shelf card without fetching the manifest.

audience.description: Content self-rating, verified at review (mirrors every other kind's own `audience`). The app's own audience posture separately governs the SPOTS it writes — an `everyone` pack still airs under a `mature` station's rules and vice versa — so rate the briefs' own text here, not the station.

added.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) this entry was added to the catalog. `format: date` alone is annotation-only in draft-07 by default, so `pattern` carries the shape enforcement — but pattern alone only checks digit counts, not calendar validity; tools/validate.py separately parses this value with datetime.date.fromisoformat to reject a shape-valid but non-existent date.

bestFor.description: Optional use-case hints ("small town", "starter", "late night") — mirrors every other kind's own `bestFor`.
